report: Read all 22 verses end to end against the candidate table and the added units. Every multi-treatment bucket is ASV-driven: the waw takes whatever connective the ASV wrote (and/but/So/Yea/also/that/And that), the pronominal suffixes take the pronoun written for them, and the assimilated article is unrepresented where the ASV writes 'a' (14.2, 14.7) and takes 'the' where it writes one (14.8).

Supplied English is treated one way throughout: a connective or subordinator over an asyndetic colon is added (14.5 'And', 14.9 'Yet', 14.11 'As'), a supplied object 'it' with no object morpheme is added (14.21 twice), a supplied 'again' is added (14.14), and a phrasal particle restating a direction the clause writes stays with the verb (14.2 'forth', 14.6 'away', 14.19 'away', 14.20 'away', 14.17 'up', 14.11 'up').

מִי יִתֵּן is read two ways because the ASV renders it two ways: literally in 14.4 ('Who can bring', split) and as the optative idiom in 14.13 ('Oh that', noncompositional with the distributed 'That' over the two asyndetic clauses under its scope, rule 25; the competing added-subordinator reading is named in the note). Not a split.
וְאוּלָם → 'But' (14.18) fused under rule 30 headed on the adverb, beside כִּי־עַתָּה → 'But now' (14.16) split because two words are written; both follow the one-rendering condition.

14.1 gives the 'of' of 'of few days' and 'full of trouble' to the construct rectum under rule 19 since MACULA tags both adjectives construct; rule 33's 'full of' valency sentence governs a bare complement with no construct relation, so this is not a conflict, and the competing head is noted.

BSB disagreements: 14.13 לִי ('appoint me a set time') and 14.17 עַל ('fastenest up mine iniquity') are both rule-40 recastings where the ASV writes nothing for the preposition's own relation; neither is an error.
The three repeated notes restate rules 15, 24 and 29; no convention, promotion or amendment is warranted.
